title: Sequenced Span Hyperview
creator: Aisha Patel
description: High-level design spec for a compact, multi-scale trace exploration surface called 'Sequenced Span Hyperview' — aimed at fast drill-downs from fleet-level latency anomalies into per-request span timelines, with correlation ID fan-out, lightweight playback, and shareable snapshot links.
problem_statement: Operators and engineers need to investigate perf regressions quickly without switching tools: current console tracing UIs require many clicks to surface cross-service causal paths and to compare similar requests side-by-side. We need a single, compact workspace optimized for rapid hypothesis generation and sharing.
goals: 1) Provide a low-friction path from alert -> correlated request set -> single-request deep dive. 2) Enable temporal playback and scrubbing across correlated spans. 3) Allow ephemeral sharing and pinning of span snapshots for debugging. 4) Keep memory/CPU overhead low for the Console when rendering high-density traces.
user_stories: As an SRE I want to scrub a 60s window of related requests and see span timing compressed/expanded so I can spot tail latency patterns.
As an engineer I want to pin a span and propagate its correlation ID to show all related requests across services in a fan-out panel.
As a PM I want to save and share a compact snapshot link that reproduces the exact view for a postmortem.
As a frontend dev I need keyboard shortcuts to jump between spans and toggle compact mode for demos.
interaction_spec: Canvas composed of three lanes: Timeline Overview (top), Lane Grid (center), Fan-out Panel (right). Hover reveals span tooltip with tags, latency, and sampling metadata. Scrub bar controls global time window and animates lane highlights. Clicking a span opens an inline detail sheet with headers, full log snippet, and direct link to raw trace. Ctrl/Cmd+P pins span to top; pinned spans persist in URL query param.
animations_and_performance: Playback uses requestAnimationFrame with 60fps cap; heavy rendering routes to canvas layers to avoid DOM thrashing. For >500 spans, automatically switch to density aggregation where spans are drawn as heatbars. Use progressive hydration: initial lightweight SVGs then replace with detailed HTML on demand.
telemetry_schema_notes: Include sample_rate, correlation_id, selected_time_range, visible_span_count, user_action origin (alert/console/search). Events must be low-cardinality where possible.
accessibility_notes: Keyboard navigation for scrubbing (left/right), focusable spans with aria-describedby linking to tooltip content, high-contrast mode for heatbars, screen-reader summary of currently selected span sequence. Color choices tested for WCAG AA contrast.
microcopy_guidelines: Span tooltip title: <service> · <operation>. Latency label uses 'p99'/'p50'. Share snapshot modal warns: 'Snapshot includes trace metadata but not raw logs unless you enable full export.'
tradeoffs: Dense visualizations increase cognitive load — default to compact aggregation and require an 'Expand to full detail' action. Snapshot links are convenient but increase risk of stale context; include timestamp and model-version metadata where applicable.
review_comments: PM: Prefer default to compact aggregation to reduce noise for first-time users (Aisha 2025-02-18)
Eng: Canvas layer approach looks good but verify memory profile on Safari iOS (Diego 2025-02-21)
Security: Snapshot links must expire by default; add option to require SSO before viewing (Priya 2025-02-25)
Design: Consider 'auto-correlate' toggle so users can opt-out of cross-service fanout (Marco 2025-03-01)
decisions_made: 1) Use progressive rendering with canvas fallback for large traces. 2) Snapshot links expire after 7 days by default. 3) Fan-out panel will surface up to 50 related requests and provide 'Load more' for deeper exploration.
open_questions: Should snapshots include anonymized payload samples by default?
What guardrails do we need for pinning many spans into a single snapshot?
Do we allow inline editable annotations on snapshots or make annotations part of Postmortem only?
next_steps: Eng spike to validate canvas memory usage on Chrome/Safari (owner: Diego) - due 2025-03-07
Add snapshot expiry option to API contract and spec with Security (owner: Priya) - due 2025-03-09
Conduct 3 usability sessions with SREs to validate compact defaults (owner: Aisha) - due 2025-03-11
Finalize keyboard shortcut mapping and add to global shortcuts reference (owner: Marco) - due 2025-03-12
acceptance_criteria: Open prototype reproduces timeline + fan-out for sample traces in staging dataset
Playback scrubbing latency <120ms for 200 visible spans on tested browsers
Snapshot link generator returns URL that reproduces same view within 7 days
Accessibility keyboard flows pass internal audit for span selection and scrubbing
notes_for_engineering: Provide a small mock dataset (1000 traces) and a feature-flagged rollout to test memory and telemetry impact. Expose a render-mode flag (compact|expanded|aggregated) in the API so the Console can request a preferred density.
